# Three.js Animation — Particles, Shaders, Globes, Scroll

Focused on the aesthetics and techniques behind atmospheric, particle-driven, scroll-linked WebGL scenes.

## Setup Boilerplate

Every scene starts here. Get this right before anything else.

```js
import * as THREE from 'three'
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js'
import { EffectComposer } from 'three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js'
import { RenderPass } from 'three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/RenderPass.js'
import { UnrealBloomPass } from 'three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/UnrealBloomPass.js'

const scene = new THREE.Scene()
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, innerWidth / innerHeight, 0.1, 1000)
camera.position.z = 3

const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true })
renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight)
renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2)) // always clamp DPR
renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping
renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.0
document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement)

// Resize handler
window.addEventListener('resize', () => {
  camera.aspect = innerWidth / innerHeight
  camera.updateProjectionMatrix()
  renderer.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight)
  composer?.setSize(innerWidth, innerHeight)
})

const clock = new THREE.Clock()
```

## Particle Systems

### Basic starfield (BufferGeometry + Points)

```js
function createStarfield(count = 5000) {
  const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
  const positions = new Float32Array(count * 3)
  const sizes = new Float32Array(count)

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    positions[i * 3]     = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 20  // x
    positions[i * 3 + 1] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 20  // y
    positions[i * 3 + 2] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 20  // z
    sizes[i] = Math.random() * 2 + 0.5
  }

  geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3))
  geometry.setAttribute('size', new THREE.BufferAttribute(sizes, 1))

  const material = new THREE.PointsMaterial({
    color: 0xffffff,
    size: 0.02,
    sizeAttenuation: true,
    transparent: true,
    opacity: 0.8,
  })

  return new THREE.Points(geometry, material)
}

scene.add(createStarfield())
```

### Custom shader particles (glow, color variation, motion)

```glsl
// vertexShader
attribute float size;
attribute vec3 color;
varying vec3 vColor;
varying float vAlpha;

void main() {
  vColor = color;
  vec4 mvPosition = modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
  gl_PointSize = size * (300.0 / -mvPosition.z);
  gl_Position = projectionMatrix * mvPosition;
  vAlpha = clamp(1.0 - length(position) / 10.0, 0.0, 1.0);
}
```

```glsl
// fragmentShader
varying vec3 vColor;
varying float vAlpha;

void main() {
  // Circular soft particle
  float dist = length(gl_PointCoord - vec2(0.5));
  if (dist > 0.5) discard;
  float alpha = 1.0 - smoothstep(0.3, 0.5, dist);
  gl_FragColor = vec4(vColor, alpha * vAlpha);
}
```

```js
const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
  vertexShader,
  fragmentShader,
  uniforms: {
    uTime: { value: 0 },
  },
  transparent: true,
  depthWrite: false,
  blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, // key for nebula/glow look
})
```

### Animated particles (turbulence, drift)

```js
// In animate loop — mutate position buffer each frame
function updateParticles(geometry, time) {
  const positions = geometry.attributes.position.array

  for (let i = 0; i < positions.length; i += 3) {
    positions[i + 1] += Math.sin(time + positions[i] * 0.5) * 0.001 // gentle y drift
  }

  geometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true
}
```

## GLSL Shader Patterns

### ShaderMaterial template

```js
const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
  uniforms: {
    uTime:       { value: 0 },
    uResolution: { value: new THREE.Vector2(innerWidth, innerHeight) },
    uMouse:      { value: new THREE.Vector2(0.5, 0.5) },
    uTexture:    { value: null },
  },
  vertexShader: `
    varying vec2 vUv;
    void main() {
      vUv = uv;
      gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
    }
  `,
  fragmentShader: `
    uniform float uTime;
    uniform vec2 uResolution;
    varying vec2 vUv;

    void main() {
      vec3 color = vec3(vUv, sin(uTime) * 0.5 + 0.5);
      gl_FragColor = vec4(color, 1.0);
    }
  `,
})

// Update time in loop
material.uniforms.uTime.value = clock.getElapsedTime()
```

### Atmospheric fog / nebula shader (plane overlay)

```glsl
// fragmentShader — noise-based fog
uniform float uTime;
varying vec2 vUv;

float hash(vec2 p) {
  return fract(sin(dot(p, vec2(127.1, 311.7))) * 43758.5453);
}

float noise(vec2 p) {
  vec2 i = floor(p);
  vec2 f = fract(p);
  f = f * f * (3.0 - 2.0 * f);
  return mix(
    mix(hash(i), hash(i + vec2(1,0)), f.x),
    mix(hash(i + vec2(0,1)), hash(i + vec2(1,1)), f.x),
    f.y
  );
}

float fbm(vec2 p) {
  float v = 0.0;
  float a = 0.5;
  for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    v += a * noise(p);
    p *= 2.0;
    a *= 0.5;
  }
  return v;
}

void main() {
  vec2 uv = vUv * 3.0 + vec2(uTime * 0.05);
  float fog = fbm(uv);
  vec3 color = mix(vec3(0.0, 0.05, 0.15), vec3(0.3, 0.5, 0.8), fog);
  gl_FragColor = vec4(color, fog * 0.6);
}
```

## Globe / Sphere Systems

### Particle globe (points distributed on sphere surface)

```js
function createParticleGlobe(radius = 2, count = 3000) {
  const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
  const positions = new Float32Array(count * 3)

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    // Uniform sphere distribution (Fibonacci spiral)
    const phi   = Math.acos(1 - (2 * (i + 0.5)) / count)
    const theta = Math.PI * (1 + Math.sqrt(5)) * i

    positions[i * 3]     = radius * Math.sin(phi) * Math.cos(theta)
    positions[i * 3 + 1] = radius * Math.cos(phi)
    positions[i * 3 + 2] = radius * Math.sin(phi) * Math.sin(theta)
  }

  geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3))

  const material = new THREE.PointsMaterial({
    color: 0x88aaff,
    size: 0.015,
    sizeAttenuation: true,
    transparent: true,
    opacity: 0.7,
    blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending,
  })

  return new THREE.Points(geometry, material)
}

const globe = createParticleGlobe()
scene.add(globe)

// Rotate in loop
globe.rotation.y += delta * 0.3
```

### Sphere with atmosphere shader

```js
// Inner sphere
const sphereGeo = new THREE.SphereGeometry(2, 64, 64)
const sphereMat = new THREE.MeshPhongMaterial({
  color: 0x112244,
  emissive: 0x001133,
  transparent: true,
  opacity: 0.9,
})
scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(sphereGeo, sphereMat))

// Atmosphere glow (larger sphere, additive blend)
const atmGeo = new THREE.SphereGeometry(2.15, 64, 64)
const atmMat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
  uniforms: { glowColor: { value: new THREE.Color(0x4488ff) } },
  vertexShader: `
    varying float intensity;
    void main() {
      vec3 vNormal = normalize(normalMatrix * normal);
      intensity = pow(0.6 - dot(vNormal, vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)), 2.0);
      gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);
    }
  `,
  fragmentShader: `
    uniform vec3 glowColor;
    varying float intensity;
    void main() {
      gl_FragColor = vec4(glowColor, intensity);
    }
  `,
  side: THREE.BackSide,
  blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending,
  transparent: true,
})
scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(atmGeo, atmMat))
```

## Post-Processing (Bloom / Glow)

Essential for the nebula/atmospheric look.

```js
import { EffectComposer } from 'three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js'
import { RenderPass } from 'three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/RenderPass.js'
import { UnrealBloomPass } from 'three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/UnrealBloomPass.js'

const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer)
composer.addPass(new RenderPass(scene, camera))

const bloom = new UnrealBloomPass(
  new THREE.Vector2(innerWidth, innerHeight),
  1.5,   // strength (0–3, start at 1.0–1.5)
  0.4,   // radius
  0.85   // threshold (lower = more blooms)
)
composer.addPass(bloom)

// Use composer.render() instead of renderer.render() in loop
function animate() {
  requestAnimationFrame(animate)
  const delta = clock.getDelta()

  // update scene...
  composer.render()
}
```

## Scroll-Linked 3D Animation

Integrate GSAP ScrollTrigger with Three.js camera/scene.

```js
// npm install gsap
import gsap from 'gsap'
import { ScrollTrigger } from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger'
gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)

// Create a tall scroll container
document.body.style.height = '400vh'

// Camera moves as user scrolls
const scrollState = { progress: 0 }

ScrollTrigger.create({
  start: 0,
  end: 'max',
  onUpdate: (self) => {
    scrollState.progress = self.progress
  },
})

// Apply in animation loop (smooth lerp to avoid jitter)
let currentZ = 3
function animate() {
  requestAnimationFrame(animate)
  const delta = clock.getDelta()
  const targetZ = 3 - scrollState.progress * 6

  // Smooth follow
  currentZ += (targetZ - currentZ) * 0.05
  camera.position.z = currentZ

  // Rotate globe on scroll
  if (globe) globe.rotation.y = scrollState.progress * Math.PI * 2

  composer.render()
}
```

### Section-based camera keyframes

```js
const cameraPath = [
  { z: 5, y: 0, x: 0 },      // section 0
  { z: 2, y: 1, x: -1 },     // section 1
  { z: 3, y: -0.5, x: 2 },   // section 2
  { z: 1, y: 0, x: 0 },      // section 3
]

ScrollTrigger.create({
  start: 0,
  end: 'max',
  onUpdate: (self) => {
    const p = self.progress * (cameraPath.length - 1)
    const i = Math.floor(p)
    const t = p - i
    const from = cameraPath[Math.min(i, cameraPath.length - 1)]
    const to   = cameraPath[Math.min(i + 1, cameraPath.length - 1)]

    camera.position.x = from.x + (to.x - from.x) * t
    camera.position.y = from.y + (to.y - from.y) * t
    camera.position.z = from.z + (to.z - from.z) * t
    camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0)
  },
})
```

## React / Next.js Integration

```jsx
'use client'
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'
import * as THREE from 'three'

export function ThreeScene() {
  const mountRef = useRef(null)

  useEffect(() => {
    const mount = mountRef.current
    const scene = new THREE.Scene()
    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, mount.clientWidth / mount.clientHeight, 0.1, 1000)
    camera.position.z = 3

    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true })
    renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2))
    renderer.setSize(mount.clientWidth, mount.clientHeight)
    mount.appendChild(renderer.domElement)

    const clock = new THREE.Clock()
    let animId

    function animate() {
      animId = requestAnimationFrame(animate)
      // update scene
      renderer.render(scene, camera)
    }
    animate()

    const handleResize = () => {
      camera.aspect = mount.clientWidth / mount.clientHeight
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix()
      renderer.setSize(mount.clientWidth, mount.clientHeight)
    }
    window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize)

    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(animId)
      window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize)
      renderer.dispose()
      mount.removeChild(renderer.domElement)
    }
  }, [])

  return <div ref={mountRef} style={{ width: '100%', height: '100vh' }} />
}
```

---

## Performance Rules

1. **Clamp DPR** — `Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2)` always
2. **AdditiveBlending + depthWrite: false** — for particles/glow overlays
3. **BufferGeometry only** — never legacy Geometry
4. **Reuse geometries and materials** — don't recreate in loop
5. **Instanced mesh** for 1000+ identical objects (`THREE.InstancedMesh`)
6. **Dispose on unmount** — `geometry.dispose()`, `material.dispose()`, `renderer.dispose()`
7. **Pause when hidden** — stop RAF loop if tab not visible (`document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', ...)`)
8. **Bloom is expensive** — tune `threshold` up to reduce affected objects; keep `strength` ≤ 2

---

## Reduced Motion

```js
const prefersReduced = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches

function animate() {
  requestAnimationFrame(animate)
  if (!prefersReduced) {
    particles.rotation.y += delta * 0.1
    material.uniforms.uTime.value = clock.getElapsedTime()
  }
  composer.render()
}
```

# DESIGN.md — Ultraterrestrial Research Canvas (Microfilm Dark)

Codified 2026-07-08 from `apps/app/src/components/design-system/{ARCHIVAL_DYSTOPIAN_AESTHETIC,RESEARCH_CANVAS_AESTHETIC,DESIGN_SYSTEM}.md` plus the live canvas chrome. Register: **product**.

## Scene

A researcher at 23:00 in a dim room, arranging declassified records on a large monitor. The canvas is the reading table; panels are documents pulled into the lamplight. Dark is forced by the scene: the luminous graph is the subject, chrome recedes into the desk.

## Concept

**Microfilm Dark**: the archival dossier aesthetic (manila, typewriter, stamps, redaction) photographed at night. Not neon cyberpunk; HUD elements are digital ghosts at low opacity. Institutional, clinical, slightly ominous.

## Color (OKLCH, warm-tinted toward manila hue ≈85)

Strategy: Restrained neutrals + a semantic evidentiary palette (data-viz exception).

| Token | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `--ut-void` | `oklch(0.16 0.006 85)` | canvas base |
| `--ut-surface` | `oklch(0.21 0.008 85 / 0.88)` | panel base (dark manila glass) |
| `--ut-surface-2` | `oklch(0.25 0.01 85 / 0.9)` | raised layer (tooltips, chips) |
| `--ut-line` | `oklch(0.87 0.02 85 / 0.14)` | hairlines |
| `--ut-paper` | `oklch(0.93 0.015 90)` | primary text (never #fff) |
| `--ut-ink-dim` | `oklch(0.93 0.015 90 / 0.62)` | secondary text |
| `--ut-ink-faint` | `oklch(0.93 0.015 90 / 0.4)` | tertiary/meta text |
| `--ut-stamp` | `oklch(0.58 0.19 27)` | stamped red — classification, Disconfirmed |

Semantic evidentiary hues (existing, kept): emerald = documented/observed, violet = AI/resonant, amber = temporal/contested, zinc = unverified, red = disconfirmed.

**Provenance delineation rule**: solid borders = sourced/deterministic content; **dashed borders = AI inference** (the analytical layer, per the terminology ruling). Never mix.

## Typography

- UI labels, meta, stamps, badges: **Martian Mono** (`--font-martian-mono`), uppercase, 9–10px, tracking 0.12–0.16em. This is the OCR/teletype voice.
- Body/prose in panels: existing sans stack, 11–12.5px.
- **Special Elite** (`--font-special-elite`): ONE wordmark moment per surface (the dossier panel title). Never in buttons, data, or repeated labels.

## Signature elements (the hallmark set)

1. **Clipped dossier corner** — `clip-path` 12px diagonal cut on the top-right of major panels ("secret-file cuts").
2. **Bracketed evidentiary badges** — `[ CORROBORATED ]` in mono; the UI mirrors the wire format (`[State]` prefixes in edge reasoning). Provenance made visible.
3. **Redaction-bar skeletons** — loading states are redacted lines that "declassify" into text. Never spinners inside content.
4. **File-reference micro-header** — `UT·RC // N:07 · E:05` mono metadata line on dossier panels.

## Texture

Film grain (inline SVG feTurbulence, ~5% opacity) + warm dot grid on the canvas + soft vignette. No scanlines, no glassmorphism-as-default, no glow bloom.

## Motion

State only: 150–250ms ease-out transitions; existing spring panel entries kept; redaction shimmer only while loading. No decorative loops.

## Bans (inherited + local)

Side-stripe borders (`border-l-2` accents), gradient text, hero-metric blocks, identical card grids, cheap meta-labels ("SECTION 01"), display fonts in controls, neon above 15% surface share.

The CSS approach nests content hierarchically so that deeper layers visually nest inside parent cards through grid row positioning, creating the illusion of depth while keeping everything in the DOM.

For the layout, I'm using a grid structure where each layer has a header band and content region, with nested layers positioned in the second grid row and offset by padding at each depth level. When the stack explodes, nested layers translate in Z-space with compounding offsets. I'll design each layer as a dossier panel with a header row containing labels and badges, then body content that gets progressively inset as nesting deepens. So the nested layers sit on top of the body slot area—each level shows its own header plus an empty frame where the next layer's content appears. The innermost layer (the status list) is fully rendered, while the outer layers just show headers and slot frames with the nested content overlaid on top.

When collapsed, you see the staircase effect: the main header at the top, then the event record header below it, then the status content below that. When exploded, each layer separates to reveal the full table underneath. The key is that each deeper layer starts one header-height lower, creating that cascading visual effect.

For the content structure, I'm planning four data layers plus the base: the case file header at the top, then the event record with its facts grid, the personnel section with the witness table, the evidence section with documents, and finally the analysis layer at the deepest level.

The key insight is that when collapsed, you see all the headers stacked with the analysis content visible on top—like a dossier where the deepest layer sits frontmost. For the height calculations, I'll anchor everything to a fixed height for the core analysis content and let each parent layer's height cascade naturally from its header plus the space needed for its child layers below.

The tricky part is managing when the parent body content (like a table) might be taller than the nested stack. I'll use `height: 100%` with `overflow: hidden` on the bodies so they stay compact and fit within their grid cells, letting the union of the body and nested layer determine the final cell size. This keeps the staircase effect clean without awkward gaps.

For the concrete sizing with a 44px heading, each layer's row-2 cell needs to accommodate the heading plus the core content size (around 200px) plus whatever nested layers sit below it. Every body gets designed to fit exactly within its allocated space, and the grid cell naturally grows to whatever height the deepest nested layer chain requires.

Now I'm mapping out the interactions: toggling explode mode, dragging to orbit the structure when expanded by adjusting yaw and pitch values, a depth slider to control how many layers show, hover effects that lift and dim shadows using CSS selectors, and clicking a layer header to select it and show a side panel with linked records and their states. I'll keep the info rail simple and fixed on the right, updating as you hover or click. Reduced motion mode will snap transitions instantly, and the controls themselves will follow the Microfilm H styling.

For the route page, I'm wrapping a client-side RecordStack component with server-side data, adding a title and description in the Microfilm voice. export type EvidentiaryState =
  | 'CORROBORATED'
  | 'DOCUMENTED'
  | 'CONTESTED'
  | 'UNVERIFIED'
  | 'DISCONFIRMED'
  | 'AI-INFERRED'

export interface RecordLink {
  ref: string
  label: string
  state: EvidentiaryState
}

export interface EventLayerData {
  kind: 'event'
  facts: Array<{ term: string; detail: string }>
}

export interface PersonnelLayerData {
  kind: 'personnel'
  witnesses: Array<{
    name: string
    role: string
    testimony: EvidentiaryState
  }>
}

export interface EvidenceLayerData {
  kind: 'evidence'
  items: Array<{
    name: string
    provenance: string
    state: EvidentiaryState
  }>
}

export interface AnalysisLayerData {
  kind: 'analysis'
  hypotheses: Array<{ label: string; state: EvidentiaryState }>
  anomalyIndex: string
  falsifiability: string
}

export type LayerBody =
  | EventLayerData
  | PersonnelLayerData
  | EvidenceLayerData
  | AnalysisLayerData

export interface StackLayer {
  id: string
  /** uppercase mono label shown in the layer heading band */
  label: string
  state: EvidentiaryState
  /** one-line summary shown in the inspector rail */
  summary: string
  /** records in the wider web this layer connects to */
  links: RecordLink[]
  body: LayerBody
}

export interface CaseStackData {
  fileRef: string
  classification: string
  title: string
  subtitle: string
  /** ordered outermost (case shell) -> innermost (analysis) */
  layers: StackLayer[]
}

I'm setting up the CSS structure scoped to `.ut-stack-scene` with nested divs for the stage and root container, including shadow elements for depth.

The markup organizes layers recursively — the outermost dossier shell at depth 0, then the four data layers (event, personnel, evidence, analysis) nested beneath it, creating a five-layer stack where the analysis layer sits visually on top, revealing the sourced record underneath when expanded. The grid geometry for `.ut-layer` is coming next to handle the layout. Relying on DOM order and a tiny negative translateZ to keep the shadow behind the content in both 3D and flat views. Setting up the content grid to match the parent's row structure, then nesting layers below the header with appropriate padding and inset spacing.

For the exploded view, I'm configuring rotation angles and translation offsets on the stack scene, applying preserve-3d throughout the hierarchy, and using a data attribute to trigger the 3D transforms with a smooth transition.

When exploded, the main container rotates first while nested layers translate outward with a staggered delay, and when collapsing, the order reverses so layers gather before the main rotation completes. On hover, I'm lifting the content and shadow elements slightly with a translate effect.

For shadow dimming, I'm using the `:has()` selector to detect when a nested mover is hovered and fade the surrounding shadows to create depth. Selected layers get a subtle outline highlight, and the scene itself uses a dark void background with a dot grid pattern, vignette, and grain texture overlay. The stage centers everything with grid layout, and controls are positioned at the bottom.

The inspector panel sits as a fixed rail on the right side in monospace font. I'm respecting reduced motion preferences by cutting transition durations to nearly instant. When dragging, I'm disabling transitions on the stack root and switching to a grabbing cursor. For typography, I'm using Martian Mono as the default monospace with JetBrains Mono as fallback, and a special serif font for the wordmark. State colors map to semantic meanings—emerald for corroborated information, amber for contested claims, and zinc for unverified data.

/* Record Stack — 3D exploding dossier anatomy (Microfilm Dark)
   Technique after jh3y's "3D CSS Grid Exploding Stack": recursive nested
   layers with preserve-3d so per-layer Z translates compound on explode. */

.ut-stack-scene {
  /* Microfilm Dark tokens (DESIGN.md) */
  --ut-void: oklch(0.16 0.006 85);
  --ut-surface: oklch(0.21 0.008 85);
  --ut-surface-2: oklch(0.25 0.01 85);
  --ut-line: oklch(0.87 0.02 85 / 0.14);
  --ut-paper: oklch(0.93 0.015 90);
  --ut-ink-dim: oklch(0.93 0.015 90 / 0.62);
  --ut-ink-faint: oklch(0.93 0.015 90 / 0.4);
  --ut-stamp: oklch(0.58 0.19 27);
  --ut-emerald: oklch(0.72 0.14 160);
  --ut-violet: oklch(0.72 0.12 300);
  --ut-amber: oklch(0.78 0.13 80);
  --ut-zinc: oklch(0.7 0.01 85);
  --ut-shadow: oklch(0 0 0 / 0.65);
  --mono: var(--font-martian-mono, 'JetBrains Mono', 'Martian Mono'), monospace;

  /* stack geometry */
  --heading: 46px;
  --core-h: 236px;
  --inset: 0.9rem;
  --radius: 10px;

  /* explode config (driven from JS) */
  --x1: -20;
  --y1: 35;
  --x2: 30;
  --step: 3.2;
  --tx: 0.5;
  --ty: -0.5;

  /* custom power easing (jh3y) */
  --power: linear(
    0 0%, 0.2688 9.91%, 0.3859 15%, 0.4917 20.19%, 0.5865 25.5%,
    0.6705 30.93%, 0.7441 36.51%, 0.8075 42.26%, 0.8593 47.98%,
    0.9022 53.93%, 0.9366 60.13%, 0.963 66.67%, 0.9812 73.4%,
    0.9929 80.76%, 0.9986 88.89%, 1 100%
  );

  position: relative;
  min-height: 100svh;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  overflow: hidden;
  background: var(--ut-void);
  color: var(--ut-paper);
  font-family: var(--mono);
}

/* warm dot grid + vignette backdrop */
.ut-stack-scene::before {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  background-image: radial-gradient(
    oklch(0.87 0.02 85 / 0.1) 1px,
    transparent 1px
  );
  background-size: 26px 26px;
  mask-image: radial-gradient(ellipse 90% 80% at 50% 45%, white 30%, transparent 75%);
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* 3D machinery                                                        */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

.ut-stack {
  transform-style: preserve-3d;
  cursor: grab;
}
.ut-stack *,
.ut-stack::before {
  transform-style: preserve-3d;
}
.ut-stack[data-dragging='true'] {
  cursor: grabbing;
}

.ut-stack {
  width: clamp(320px, 46vw, 540px);
  display: grid;
  grid-template: auto / auto;
  transition: transform 1s var(--power);
}

.ut-stack[data-exploded='false'] {
  transform: rotateX(0deg) rotateY(0deg) rotateX(0deg);
  transition-delay: 0.9s;
}
.ut-stack[data-exploded='true'] {
  transform: rotateX(calc(var(--x1) * 1deg)) rotateY(calc(var(--y1) * 1deg))
    rotateX(calc(var(--x2) * 1deg));
  transition-delay: 0s;
}
.ut-stack[data-dragging='true'] {
  transition: none;
}

/* each layer: heading band + body region; nested layer overlays the body */
.ut-stack .layer {
  pointer-events: none;
  position: relative;
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: var(--heading) 1fr;
  translate: 0 0 0;
  transition: translate 1s var(--power);
}
.ut-stack[data-exploded='false'] .layer {
  transition-delay: 0s;
}
.ut-stack[data-exploded='true'] .layer--nested {
  translate: calc(var(--tx) * 1rem) calc(var(--ty) * 1rem)
    calc(var(--step) * 1rem);
  transition-delay: 0.9s;
}
.ut-stack[data-dragging='true'] .layer {
  transition: none;
}

.ut-stack .layer--nested {
  grid-area: 2 / 1;
  padding: 0 var(--inset) var(--inset);
}

.ut-stack .mover {
  pointer-events: all;
  grid-area: 1 / 1 / -1 / -1;
  display: grid;
  grid-template: auto / auto;
}
.ut-stack .mover > * {
  grid-area: 1 / 1;
}

/* content card: heading + body rows matching the section grid */
.ut-stack .content {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: var(--heading) 1fr;
  background: var(--ut-surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--ut-line);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  transition: transform 0.26s;
  min-width: 0;
}
.ut-stack[data-exploded='true'] .mover:hover > .content,
.ut-stack[data-exploded='true'] .mover:hover > .card-shadow {
  transform: translate3d(0, 0, 1.1rem);
}
.ut-stack .mover:focus-within > .content {
  outline: 1px dashed var(--ut-ink-faint);
  outline-offset: 3px;
}

/* drop shadows: fade/scale away as siblings lift, spread on explode */
.ut-stack .card-shadow {
  pointer-events: none;
  opacity: 0.35;
  scale: 0.999;
  transition: opacity 1s, transform 0.26s, scale 0.26s;
}
.ut-stack .card-shadow > div {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  background: var(--ut-shadow);
  transition: translate 1s var(--power), scale 0.26s;
}
.ut-stack .card-shadow {
  position: relative;
  z-index: -1;
}
.ut-stack[data-exploded='true'] .card-shadow {
  opacity: 0.55;
}
.ut-stack[data-exploded='true'] .card-shadow > div {
  translate: calc(var(--tx) * 1.4rem) calc(var(--ty) * -1.4rem);
  transition-delay: 0.9s;
}
/* dim ancestor shadows while a deeper layer is hovered */
.ut-stack .mover:has(+ .layer .mover:hover) > .card-shadow {
  opacity: 0.15;
}
.ut-stack .mover:has(+ .layer .mover:hover) > .card-shadow > div {
  scale: 0.94;
}
.ut-stack[data-exploded='true'] .mover:hover > .card-shadow {
  opacity: 0.8;
  scale: 0.98;
}

/* selected layer accent */
.ut-stack .mover[data-selected='true'] > .content {
  border-color: oklch(0.87 0.02 85 / 0.35);
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Dossier chrome                                                      */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

.ut-stack .layer-heading {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.6rem;
  padding: 0 0.9rem;
  font-size: 10px;
  letter-spacing: 0.14em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ut-ink-dim);
  border: 0;
  background: none;
  font-family: inherit;
  text-align: left;
  cursor: pointer;
  width: 100%;
}
.ut-stack .layer-heading .idx {
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
}
.ut-stack .layer-heading .ttl {
  color: var(--ut-paper);
  font-weight: 600;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.ut-stack .layer-heading .links {
  margin-left: auto;
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
  font-size: 9px;
  letter-spacing: 0.12em;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* bracketed evidentiary badge */
.ut-badge {
  font-size: 9px;
  letter-spacing: 0.12em;
  white-space: nowrap;
  color: var(--state, var(--ut-zinc));
}
.ut-badge::before {
  content: '[ ';
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
}
.ut-badge::after {
  content: ' ]';
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
}
[data-state='CORROBORATED'],
[data-state='DOCUMENTED'] {
  --state: var(--ut-emerald);
}
[data-state='CONTESTED'] {
  --state: var(--ut-amber);
}
[data-state='UNVERIFIED'] {
  --state: var(--ut-zinc);
}
[data-state='DISCONFIRMED'] {
  --state: var(--ut-stamp);
}
[data-state='AI-INFERRED'] {
  --state: var(--ut-violet);
}

/* case shell: clipped dossier corner + extraction slot */
.ut-stack .content--case {
  clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 14px) 0, 100% 14px, 100% 100%, 0 100%);
  background: var(--ut-surface-2);
}
.ut-stack .content--case .case-head {
  display: grid;
  align-content: center;
  gap: 2px;
  padding: 0 0.9rem;
}
.ut-stack .case-fileref {
  font-size: 9px;
  letter-spacing: 0.16em;
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
  text-transform: uppercase;
  display: flex;
  gap: 0.75rem;
}
.ut-stack .case-fileref .classif {
  color: var(--ut-stamp);
}
.ut-stack .case-title {
  font-family: var(--font-special-elite, var(--mono));
  font-size: 15px;
  letter-spacing: 0.02em;
  color: var(--ut-paper);
}
.ut-stack .slot-frame {
  margin: 0 var(--inset) var(--inset);
  border-radius: 6px;
  border: 1px solid oklch(0.58 0.19 27 / 0.55);
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(
    -45deg,
    transparent 0 5px,
    oklch(0.58 0.19 27 / 0.28) 5px 6px
  );
  position: relative;
}
.ut-stack .slot-frame::after {
  content: 'RECORD EXTRACTED';
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  font-size: 9px;
  letter-spacing: 0.2em;
  color: oklch(0.58 0.19 27 / 0.8);
  background: var(--ut-surface-2);
  width: max-content;
  height: max-content;
  margin: auto;
  padding: 0.2rem 0.6rem;
  border: 1px solid oklch(0.58 0.19 27 / 0.55);
  border-radius: 4px;
  rotate: -4deg;
}

/* generic layer body */
.ut-stack .layer-body {
  margin: 0 var(--inset) var(--inset);
  border-radius: 6px;
  background: var(--ut-void);
  border: 1px solid var(--ut-line);
  overflow: hidden;
  min-height: 0;
  font-size: 11px;
}

/* event facts grid */
.ut-stack .facts {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: auto 1fr;
  gap: 0.45rem 1rem;
  padding: 0.8rem 0.9rem;
  margin: 0;
}
.ut-stack .facts dt {
  font-size: 9px;
  letter-spacing: 0.14em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
  align-self: center;
}
.ut-stack .facts dd {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--ut-ink-dim);
  font-size: 10.5px;
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

/* witness table */
.ut-stack .witnesses {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
.ut-stack .witnesses td,
.ut-stack .witnesses th {
  padding: 0.42rem 0.9rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ut-line);
  font-size: 10.5px;
  text-align: left;
  font-weight: 400;
  color: var(--ut-ink-dim);
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.ut-stack .witnesses th {
  font-size: 9px;
  letter-spacing: 0.14em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
}
.ut-stack .witnesses .nm {
  color: var(--ut-paper);
}
.ut-stack .witnesses tr:last-child td {
  border-bottom: 0;
}

/* evidence list */
.ut-stack .evidence {
  list-style: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0.3rem 0;
}
.ut-stack .evidence li {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr auto;
  gap: 0 0.8rem;
  padding: 0.42rem 0.9rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ut-line);
}
.ut-stack .evidence li:last-child {
  border-bottom: 0;
}
.ut-stack .evidence .nm {
  color: var(--ut-paper);
  font-size: 10.5px;
}
.ut-stack .evidence .prov {
  grid-column: 1 / -1;
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
  font-size: 9.5px;
}

/* analysis layer — AI inference: dashed provenance boundary */
.ut-stack .content--analysis,
.ut-stack .content--analysis .layer-body {
  border-style: dashed;
}
.ut-stack .analysis {
  padding: 0.7rem 0.9rem;
  display: grid;
  gap: 0.45rem;
  height: var(--core-h);
  align-content: start;
}
.ut-stack .analysis .hyp {
  display: flex;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 0.8rem;
  color: var(--ut-ink-dim);
  font-size: 10.5px;
}
.ut-stack .analysis .metric {
  margin-top: 0.25rem;
  padding-top: 0.55rem;
  border-top: 1px dashed var(--ut-line);
  color: var(--ut-ink-dim);
  font-size: 10px;
}
.ut-stack .analysis .metric b {
  color: var(--ut-violet);
  font-weight: 600;
}
.ut-stack .analysis .falsify {
  color: var(--ut-ink-faint);
  font-size: 9.5px;
  line-height: 1.5;
}
.ut-stack .analysis .falsify::before {
  content: 'FALSIFIABILITY // ';
  color: var(--ut-amber);
  letter-spacing: 0.12em;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* HUD chrome (controls + inspector)                                   */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

.ut-stack-hud {
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  bottom: 1.4rem;
  translate: -50% 0;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 1.1rem;

  background: oklch(0.21 0.008 85 / 0.88);

}

}

}

}

}

}

/* inspector rail */

@media (max-width: 900px) {

'use client'

import { useCallback, useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type {
  CaseStackData,
  LayerBody,
  StackLayer,
} from './types'
import './record-stack.css'

const clamp = (v: number, min: number, max: number) =>
  Math.min(max, Math.max(min, v))

function LayerBodyView({ body }: { body: LayerBody }) {
  switch (body.kind) {
    case 'event':
      return (
        <dl className='facts'>
          {body.facts.map((f) => (
            <div key={f.term} style={{ display: 'contents' }}>
              <dt>{f.term}</dt>
              <dd>{f.detail}</dd>
            </div>
          ))}
        </dl>
      )
    case 'personnel':
      return (
        <table className='witnesses'>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>Name</th>
              <th>Role</th>
              <th>Testimony</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {body.witnesses.map((w) => (
              <tr key={w.name}>
                <td className='nm'>{w.name}</td>
                <td>{w.role}</td>
                <td>
                  <span className='ut-badge' data-state={w.testimony}>
                    {w.testimony}
                  </span>
                </td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      )
    case 'evidence':
      return (
        <ul className='evidence'>
          {body.items.map((item) => (
            <li key={item.name}>
              <span className='nm'>{item.name}</span>
              <span className='ut-badge' data-state={item.state}>
                {item.state}
              </span>
              <span className='prov'>{item.provenance}</span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )
    case 'analysis':
      return (
        <div className='analysis'>
          {body.hypotheses.map((h) => (
            <div className='hyp' key={h.label}>
              <span>{h.label}</span>
              <span className='ut-badge' data-state={h.state}>
                {h.state}
              </span>
            </div>
          ))}
          <div className='metric'>
            anomaly index <b>{body.anomalyIndex}</b>
          </div>
          <p className='falsify'>{body.falsifiability}</p>
        </div>
      )
  }
}

interface LayerNodeProps {
  layers: StackLayer[]
  depth: number
  selectedId: string
  onSelect: (id: string) => void
}

/** Recursive layer tree — nesting is what makes Z translates compound. */
function LayerNode({ layers, depth, selectedId, onSelect }: LayerNodeProps) {
  const [layer, ...rest] = layers
  const isAnalysis = layer.body.kind === 'analysis'
  return (
    <section className={`layer${depth > 0 ? ' layer--nested' : ''}`}>
      <div className='mover' data-selected={selectedId === layer.id}>
        <div className='card-shadow' aria-hidden='true'>
          <div />
        </div>
        <div
          className={`content${isAnalysis ? ' content--analysis' : ''}`}
        >
          <button
            type='button'
            className='layer-heading'
            onClick={() => onSelect(layer.id)}
            onPointerEnter={() => onSelect(layer.id)}
          >
            <span className='idx'>L:{String(depth + 1).padStart(2, '0')}</span>
            <span className='ttl'>{layer.label}</span>
            <span className='ut-badge' data-state={layer.state}>
              {layer.state}
            </span>
            <span className='links'>{layer.links.length} linked</span>
          </button>
          <div className='layer-body'>
            <LayerBodyView body={layer.body} />
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      {rest.length > 0 && (
        <LayerNode
          layers={rest}
          depth={depth + 1}
          selectedId={selectedId}
          onSelect={onSelect}
        />
      )}
    </section>
  )
}

export interface RecordStackProps {
  data: CaseStackData
}

export function RecordStack({ data }: RecordStackProps) {
  const [exploded, setExploded] = useState(false)
  const [step, setStep] = useState(3.2)
  const [orbit, setOrbit] = useState({ x1: -20, y1: 35, x2: 30 })
  const [dragging, setDragging] = useState(false)
  const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(data.layers[0]?.id ?? '')
  const drag = useRef<{ x: number; y: number; y1: number; x2: number } | null>(
    null,
  )

  const selected = useMemo(
    () => data.layers.find((l) => l.id === selectedId) ?? data.layers[0],
    [data.layers, selectedId],
  )

  const onPointerDown = useCallback(
    (e: React.PointerEvent) => {
      if (!exploded) return
      drag.current = {
        x: e.clientX,
        y: e.clientY,
        y1: orbit.y1,
        x2: orbit.x2,
      }
      setDragging(true)
      ;(e.currentTarget as HTMLElement).setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)
    },
    [exploded, orbit],
  )

  const onPointerMove = useCallback((e: React.PointerEvent) => {
    if (!drag.current) return
    const dx = e.clientX - drag.current.x
    const dy = e.clientY - drag.current.y
    setOrbit((o) => ({
      ...o,
      y1: clamp(drag.current!.y1 + dx * 0.25, -75, 105),
      x2: clamp(drag.current!.x2 - dy * 0.25, -20, 80),
    }))
  }, [])

  const onPointerUp = useCallback(() => {
    drag.current = null
    setDragging(false)
  }, [])

  return (
    <div className='ut-stack-scene'>
      <div
        className='ut-stack'
        data-exploded={exploded}
        data-dragging={dragging}
        onPointerDown={onPointerDown}
        onPointerMove={onPointerMove}
        onPointerUp={onPointerUp}
        onPointerCancel={onPointerUp}
        style={
          {
            '--x1': orbit.x1,
            '--y1': orbit.y1,
            '--x2': orbit.x2,
            '--step': step,
          } as React.CSSProperties
        }
      >
        {/* case shell: outermost layer of the anatomy */}
        <section className='layer'>
          <div className='mover' data-selected={false}>
            <div className='card-shadow' aria-hidden='true'>
              <div />
            </div>
            <div className='content content--case'>
              <div className='case-head'>
                <span className='case-fileref'>
                  <span>{data.fileRef} · L:{String(data.layers.length + 1).padStart(2, '0')}</span>
                  <span className='classif'>{data.classification}</span>
                </span>
                <span className='case-title'>{data.title}</span>
              </div>
              <div className='slot-frame' aria-hidden='true' />
            </div>
          </div>
          <div className='layer layer--nested'>
            <LayerNode
              layers={data.layers}
              depth={1}
              selectedId={selectedId}
              onSelect={setSelectedId}
            />
          </div>
        </section>
      </div>

      <div className='ut-stack-hud'>
        <button type='button' onClick={() => setExploded((v) => !v)}>
          {exploded ? '[ collapse ]' : '[ unpack record ]'}
        </button>
        <label>
          z-sep
          <input
            type='range'
            min={2}
            max={7}
            step={0.1}
            value={step}
            onChange={(e) => setStep(Number(e.target.value))}
          />
        </label>
        <span className='hint'>
          {exploded ? 'drag to orbit · hover a layer to lift it' : data.subtitle}
        </span>
      </div>

      {selected && (
        <aside className='ut-stack-inspector'>
          <span className='insp-ref'>
            {data.fileRef} · {selected.id.toUpperCase()}
          </span>
          <div className='insp-title'>
            <span>{selected.label}</span>
            <span className='ut-badge' data-state={selected.state}>
              {selected.state}
            </span>
          </div>
          <p className='insp-summary'>{selected.summary}</p>
          <span className='insp-web'>record web · {selected.links.length} edges</span>
          <ul className='insp-links'>
            {selected.links.map((link) => (
              <li key={link.ref}>
                <span className='ref'>{link.ref}</span>
                <span className='lbl'>
                  {link.label}
                  <span className='ut-badge' data-state={link.state}>
                    {link.state}
                  </span>
                </span>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </aside>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

```

---
name: global-css-class-collisions
description: apps/app global stylesheets clobber generic class names (.content, .layer-body, .heading) — always namespace feature CSS
metadata:
  type: project
---

apps/app ships global stylesheets (globals.css, research-ui.css, etc.) that style generic class names — `.layer-body` gets `display:flex; position:absolute`, and `.content`, `.layer`, `.heading` are also taken. New feature CSS using unprefixed generic names silently breaks (grids collapse, content escapes cards).

**Why:** Discovered 2026-07-18 building the record-stack feature — its layout collapsed until every class was renamed with a `uts-` prefix.

**How to apply:** Namespace all class names in new feature CSS (e.g. `uts-`, feature-specific prefix) and scope selectors under a root class. Related: [[research-canvas-experience-layer]].

```

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-19 02:19:25Z)**_

Done — the experience is built, running, and verified live at **http://localhost:56360/record-stack** (your port 3000 is occupied by a different project's Next 16 server, so the dev server auto-picked 56360; the preview tab is showing it now).

## What I built

**Record Anatomy** — a 3D exploding dossier stack that unpacks a case record into its evidentiary layers, directly adapting Jhey's "3D CSS Grid Exploding Stack" technique: recursively nested layers with `preserve-3d`, so each layer's Z-translate compounds through the nesting and the whole stack fans apart into an axonometric exploded view. I deliberately kept it CSS 3D rather than Three.js — the layers are real DOM, so every fact, witness row, and badge stays selectable and accessible.

It's styled entirely in **Microfilm Dark**: manila-tinted OKLCH tokens, Martian Mono uppercase labels, the clipped dossier corner, bracketed `[ CORROBORATED ]` evidentiary badges, a stamped-red "RECORD EXTRACTED" slot revealed when the record lifts out of its case shell, and dashed borders on the Analysis layer marking the AI-inference provenance boundary.

The seed case is the 2004 Nimitz "Tic Tac" encounter, unpacked into five layers: **Case shell → Event Record → Witnesses → Evidence Chain → Analysis** (ending on falsifiability, per the platform's identity). The right-hand inspector rail shows each layer's summary plus its edges into the wider record web (Gimbal, GoFast, USS Omaha, AATIP…).

**Interactions (all verified in the browser):** `[ UNPACK RECORD ]` explodes/collapses with the pen's custom `linear()` power easing and staged choreography; drag anywhere to orbit; hover a layer to lift it while sibling shadows dim (`:has()`); a z-separation slider; per-layer selection driving the inspector; reduced-motion support.

## Files

- [record-stack.tsx](apps/app/src/features/record-stack/record-stack.tsx) — recursive layer tree, orbit drag, HUD, inspector
- [record-stack.css](apps/app/src/features/record-stack/record-stack.css) — 3D machinery + Microfilm Dark chrome
- [types.ts](apps/app/src/features/record-stack/types.ts) — `CaseStackData` model (any record web can feed it)
- [nimitz-case.ts](apps/app/src/features/record-stack/data/nimitz-case.ts) — curated public-record dataset
- [index.ts](apps/app/src/features/record-stack/index.ts), [page.tsx](apps/app/src/app/(site)/record-stack/page.tsx) — exports + `/record-stack` route
- [launch.json](.claude/launch.json) — new dev-server launch config

One gotcha worth knowing (saved to memory): the app's global stylesheets clobber generic class names like `.content` and `.layer-body`, which initially collapsed the whole layout — everything is now namespaced `uts-`.

Natural next step if you want it: a server loader mapping live `@db/postgres` events (via `getAllEvents` + related personnel/documents) into `CaseStackData`, so any record in the database can be unpacked this way.
